notes: Source: official Robe Lighting user manual (Version 3.3, robelighting.com), Section 3 "Fixture exterior view" and Section 10 "Technical Specifications" > "Connection". Manual states: "DMX data in/out: Locking 3-pin and 5-pin XLR", "AC power IN: Neutrik TrueOne NAC3MPX", "Ethernet IN/Out: RJ45". DMX sockets are wired in parallel (3-pin and 5-pin duplicate the same signal, both provided for compatibility). No bandwidth "grade" is set on any port: DMX-512/RS-485 and AC power are outside the gradeable connector families, and the manual does not state a modern Ethernet speed (it explicitly cites 10BaseT for Art-Net, below the lowest available grade tier eth-100m) or a USB spec version, so grade is omitted per instructions rather than guessed. The AC inlet (Neutrik TrueOne NAC3MPX) is a locking powerCON TRUE1-family connector — mapped to "powercon" as the closest id in the allowed list. The front-panel "USB port" (item 6 in the exterior-view diagram) is confirmed to physically exist but its exact type/purpose is not detailed in the manual body (software updates are documented via a separate RS232/DMX flash cable or "Robe Universal Interface" over USB from a PC, not explicitly via this front port) — connector type USB-A is inferred, not manual-confirmed, hence flagged. Fixture is a moving-head LED wash/beam luminaire (19x RGBW LED pixels, 4°-50° zoom, pan/tilt), not rackmount (13.25 kg, IP2x, floor/truss mounted via omega brackets) — rackUnits omitted. It does not cleanly fit any provided category/type enum (it's stage lighting, not AV switching/display/audio gear); category set to "other" and type to "Other" as the closest available options. A "Wireless DMX" (CRMX by LumenRadio, 2.4GHz) version exists as an optional/alternate SKU with an added RF antenna — this is not a physical cabled I/O port and was not included.

ports.note: Manual states Art-Net runs as 10BaseT Ethernet; no exact grade enum for 10Mbit so grade omitted.

ports.name: USB port
ports.note: Front control-panel USB port shown in fixture exterior-view diagram; manual does not state its exact type/speed or purpose in detail (likely direct firmware/data access), so this is inferred from typical Robe fixture design, not explicitly confirmed in the manual text.
